item.title: Day 6: Cerro Castillo
Day 5: Cerro Castillo
Day 4: Cerro Castillo
item.description:
A much needed sleep was needed after the long drive from Patagonia National Park the night before. After making myself some breakfast and enjoying my last views of Rio Tranquillo, which I had come to consider a perfect landing spot between adventures over the last few days, it was time to say goodbye.

Own my way out, I decided to check-in with two hitchhikers by the side of the road. They turned out to be a newly wed couple on their year-long honeymoon travesing the globe looking for the best mountaineering climbs. In this moment, I didn’t realize how significant these two would be to my life over the next few days. They happened to also be heading to Cerro Castillo so I thought it a perfect chance to have some company along the way and so glad that I did.

item.title: Day 3: Patagonia National Park
item.description:
I woke up this morning in a river that overlooked the Rio Baker with the mountains in the backdrop. Not a bad way to start off the day. With some boxed wine and a full dinner last night, I was ready to start my day.

It was a slow morning of having breakfast, playing with the cats and dogs as we all sat out getting our sunshine and starting to warm up. The cats were either scrating up against the tree bark, the kitten wanting to play fight, and all of them alternating between the sun and some shade under by car.

item.title: Day 2: Puerto Rio Tranquillo & Parque Exploradores
item.description: I woke up at 6:30am this morning to catch my reservation to kayak to Rio Tranquillo’s most notable highlight - Marble Caves. It started off a bit misty, but quickly cleared off as the sun rose for sunrise. Luckily it had rained this morning, since it means that the winds don’t pick up over the water leaving us with a glassy lake.

item.title: Day 1: Coyhaique to Puerto Rio Tranquillo
item.description: After yesterday’s travels, I decided to sleep in some more today and enjoy a bit of this quiant Hostel made up of old typewriters, a fireplace, and sliding doors counter-weighted by knitted hens. I hit the road by 8AM to get a headstart on the day since I would have the long drive ahead of me. I grabbed gas at the local Copec Station and began my way down South for Puerto Rio Tranquillo, but had no idea what magic the day had in store for me.
